# Merkle fixtures

Every expected root, leaf and proof in this directory was produced by
[`@openzeppelin/merkle-tree`](https://github.com/OpenZeppelin/merkle-tree) **v1.0.8** —
the implementation ADR-0003 makes normative for tree shape. None of it was produced by
`merkle`. A fixture generated by the port under test would only prove the port
agrees with itself.

| File | Claims | What it pins |
|---|---|---|
| `claims.json` | 6 | Copied verbatim from `nutz-contracts/test/fixtures/claims.json`, so both repos pin the same tree. Its root `0x88b4…7591` is the one the Distributor's own suite verifies proofs against. **Do not regenerate it here** — re-copy it if it changes upstream. |
| `single-claim.json` | 1 | The degenerate tree: root is the leaf, proof is empty. |
| `two-claims.json` | 2 | The smallest tree with a real proof. |
| `odd-claims.json` | 5 | An odd leaf count, so the complete-binary-tree layout is unbalanced and proof lengths differ between claims. Carries `0` and `2**256-1` to exercise the 224-byte serialiser at both ends. |
| `duplicate-amounts.json` | 4 | Four accounts sharing one amount vector. Leaves stay distinct only because the account is part of the preimage. |
| `unsorted-input.json` | 6 | The `sortLeaves` landmine: claims are written in the exact reverse of their leaf-hash order. An implementation that skipped the sort, or sorted descending, builds a valid-looking tree with a wrong root. |

The five generated fixtures also carry `dump`: OpenZeppelin's own `dump()` of the same tree,
which `merkle.Tree.Dump` must reproduce — that is the `tree.json` a Bundle publishes, and a
stranger loads it with OpenZeppelin's `load()`. It is compared as parsed JSON, since `load()`
is the contract and `JSON.stringify`'s layout is not. `claims.json` has none.

`merkle`'s fixture tests discover these by glob, so dropping a new one in extends coverage
without touching Go code.

## Regenerating

The five generated fixtures come from `tooling/`, which is a Node package deliberately
kept outside the Go module: it is never run by `go test` and contributes nothing to
`go.sum` or the shipped binary (ADR-0004).

```sh
cd tooling && pnpm install && pnpm gen:fixtures
```

Output is deterministic, so a regeneration that changes a committed file is a real
signal, not noise.
